summary: Radar for 2026-11-16, with ObesityWeek ending tomorrow. Three things are fresh and solid. (1) A wave of "serious complications" coverage today: the Washington Post and Detroit News on 11-16, UK "go to A&E" pieces, and a FAERS report on slowed gut movement. This gives a timely hook for the queued "Serious Risks: How Rare?" long video, and that video should be built from the label numbers. (2) SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS (tirzepatide in teens, JAMA 11-15) is in mainstream news (CBS, Bloomberg, MedPage). It is not approved for teens, so it needs careful framing. (3) Lilly showed EloraTZP data again at ObesityWeek on 11-15: in adults with type 2 diabetes the top dose gave −23.3% vs −14.8% on tirzepatide 15 mg, plus eloralintide food-noise and craving numbers. That is a cheap refresh for our biggest earner, best done as a Short and pinned comment that point to the EloraTZP long video. It is not a new long video. CagriSema's FDA decision is expected in Q4 2026 with no PDUFA date announced. Treat it as a trigger: if it is approved, it becomes an approved-drug head-to-head against tirzepatide (REDEFINE 4: 23.0% vs 25.5%). The strongest growth remains the search-demand formats the playbook asks for: Mounjaro vs Zepbound, trial weight-loss averages plus the early-responder pattern (Medscape 11-15), Months 2–6 timeline, pen and IFU how-tos, the NAION label change, and felt symptoms (nausea with a winter hook, hair loss in women). The holiday-table Shorts are at their best window (Thanksgiving is 11-26). Keeping results after stopping is rising again on new exit-strategy coverage, and the content must stay trial-only with no tapering advice. Rejected: retatrutide 'supplier' and peptide advertorials, black-market jabs, CVS/Medicaid/pricing stories, the Bioma 'GLP-1 booster' supplement review, and semaglutide in children aged 6–12 (off-audience and semaglutide-only). I could not open the full JAMA text for SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS or the Washington Post article, so the fact-checker must pull exact numbers from the primary sources.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) serious side effects: how rare are they really? Pancreatitis, gallbladder, gut slowing and the eye warning, with label rates side by side
candidates.angle: Today's headlines ask 'the serious complications few know about'. We show each one next to its real label rate vs placebo, using the pancreatitis pairing rule (0.23 vs 0.11 per 100 years in the diabetes pool, 0.14 vs 0.15 in the weight trials), plus the warning signs that mean call now. Calm, numbers-first, and it ships the queued 'Serious Risks: How Rare?' with the 11-14 fact-check fixes.
candidates.why_now: The Washington Post (picked up by the Detroit News) published 'The serious complications of GLP-1s that few may know about' on 11-16. UK outlets ran 'go to A&E if you get one symptom' pieces the same day, and a FAERS gut-slowing study was covered on 11-16. Search for 'how rare' follows fear headlines within days. Broad, searched, and fits Lane A.
